blocks.text: Reading long technical documents on a phone is tiring when the layout was made for paper. Small fonts, wide margins and fixed line breaks force the reader to zoom and pan all the time.

A reflow engine solves this by extracting the text and laying it out again for the screen. Each paragraph becomes a block that can wrap at any width, while the original page stays available for reference.
This synthetic document has three paragraphs on the first page and two on the second page. It exists so that tests can compare the engine output with a known, exact expectation.
The second page starts with a new paragraph. Its lines are wrapped by the generator at a fixed width, just like a typeset paper would be.
